The email states: "Attached is Invoice #8841 for your annual cloud hosting renewal ($14,500). Please note our bank details have changed. Send wire transfer to our new account at First Global Bank."
 Decision Point:
 Option A: Update the vendor's banking record in your accounting software and process the $14,500 wire transfer immediately to avoid server downtime. Option B: Notice the domain mismatch (.co vs .com), pause payment, and initiate out-of-band verification. (Correct Path)

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud (Vendor Account Updates & Direct Deposit Scams): Stage 2 (The Out-of-Band Verification Call)
entries.text:
How do you verify the new banking details? Decision Point:
 Option A: Call the phone number listed at the bottom of the new invoice PDF. Option B: Call the vendor's account manager using the phone number recorded in your original signed contract directory. (Correct Path)

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud (Vendor Account Updates & Direct Deposit Scams): Red Flag Indicators & Actionable Checklist
entries.text: Urgent Banking Detail Changes: Requests to update vendor or employee bank account numbers right before payment/payroll deadlines. Domain Mismatches: Subtle variations in vendor email domains (e.g., supplier-inc.co vs. supplier-inc.com). Payment Method Shifts: Requests to switch standard payment methods to wire transfers, Zelle, or gift cards. Unverified Direct Deposit Updates: Employee requests to update payroll accounts originating from personal webmail addresses.

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: Why are independent freelancers particularly attractive targets for social engineering scams? Income unpredictability and isolation from corporate IT oversight increase vulnerability to fake client lures (Ticona, 2022).

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: A client demanding that you log into a third-party website using your personal Google or Microsoft credentials to view a project brief is a major indicator of portfolio credential harvesting. Legitimate project briefs do not require logging in with personal OAuth credentials on unverified third-party domains.

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: A prospective client offers you a $5,000 project but insists on moving communications off Upwork to Telegram before a contract is started. They offer to pay via an unverified check. What should you do? Luring freelancers off-platform removes contract enforcement and escrow protections, exposing them to payment fraud.

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: Which of the following indicate that an incoming freelance inquiry is a social engineering scam? (Select TWO) Overpayment refund demands and premature requests for administrative server credentials are key fraud indicators.

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: Escrow services on freelance platforms protect freelancers by holding client funds in a neutral account until agreed project milestones are met. Escrow ensures funds are verified and set aside before work begins, reducing non-payment risks.

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: What is the primary objective of a "Portfolio Credential Harvesting" attack targeting freelancers? Fake login portals capture credentials to compromise professional accounts and cloud repositories.

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: You receive a $2,000 advance payment check from a new client. Two days later, the client emails: "Our accountant made a mistake and sent $3,500. Please Zelle us back the $1,500 difference right away." What is the safest course of action? Fake check overpayment scams rely on the victim wiring real money before the bank discovers the deposited check is counterfeit.

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: Which domain name represents a typosquatted domain designed to trick a freelancer using Figma for client design reviews? Adding words like -verify-review.net creates a lookalike domain to capture OAuth credentials.

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: Legitimate corporate clients will routinely ask freelancers to purchase gift cards as part of their initial onboarding duties. Requesting gift card purchases during onboarding is a classic financial scam.

entries.title: Freelancer Exploitation & Client Verification
entries.text: What should a freelancer do before opening a zip file sent by a new, unverified client? Unverified attachments can contain malicious scripts or executable payloads.

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: Why do cybercriminals frequently target Virtual Assistants (VAs) in executive impersonation attacks? VAs hold central administrative access and high-level trust, making them high-value targets (Lazarus, 2024).

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: An email from a CEO requesting that a Virtual Assistant purchase $1,000 in Apple gift cards for a "client emergency" is almost certainly a social engineering scam. Requesting gift card purchases is a primary financial scam tactic; legitimate businesses do not use gift cards for emergency corporate transactions.

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: You receive a message on Telegram from your remote boss: "I am on a plane with no voice signal. Send me the MFA code that was just sent to your phone so I can access my email." What should you do? MFA tokens grant account access and must never be shared, even if the requester claims to be an executive.

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: Which of the following elements are red flags indicative of executive impersonation? (Select TWO) Prohibiting voice verification and using external webmail accounts are classic executive spoofing indicators.

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: Threat actors use psychological authority pressure to make Virtual Assistants feel that questioning an executive's request will lead to immediate firing. Fear of disciplinary action is manipulated to force VAs to bypass security checks.

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: What is "Out-of-Band (OOB) Verification" in the context of Virtual Assistant workflows? OOB verification confirms identity via a separate, trusted channel (e.g., calling a known phone number).

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: You manage the calendar for a remote Vice President. An external consultant emails asking you to add a Zoom link to the VP's calendar for a "confidential acquisition meeting." The email attachment is Meeting_Agenda.docm. What should you do? Unsolicited macro-enabled files (.docm) are common malware delivery vectors.

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: What term describes an attacker flooding a Virtual Assistant's phone with dozens of login push notifications late at night in hopes the VA will tap "Approve"? MFA fatigue exploits distraction and frustration to coerce push approvals.

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: If an executive texts you from a new, unverified phone number claiming they lost their device, you should immediately grant them full access to all company cloud drives without secondary verification. Identity must be independently verified through official channels before granting access from new devices.

entries.title: Executive Support & VA Impersonation Defense
entries.text: Why do pretexters impersonating executives create artificial time emergencies ("Need this done in 15 minutes before board meeting")? Artificial time pressure suppresses analytical thinking and security protocol adherence.

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: What is the primary goal of scammers running fake remote job outreach campaigns? Fake job scams harvest PII and run advance-fee equipment check schemes (Ravenelle et al., 2022).

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: A legitimate international company will routinely hire remote employees for high-paying roles based purely on a 10-minute text conversation on Telegram without any video or voice interviews. Text-only "interviews" on anonymous messaging apps are major indicators of recruitment fraud.

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: You are hired for a remote position. The company mails you a $3,000 check and instructs you to deposit it, keep $500 as a sign-on bonus, and wire $2,500 to an "approved software vendor." What should you do? Fake check scams rely on victims wiring real money before the bank identifies the deposited check as fraudulent.

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: Which of the following details indicate that a remote job offer may be fraudulent? (Select TWO) Requesting bank passwords and using lookalike email domains indicate recruitment fraud.

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: Legitimate employers require new hires to pay application fees or background check fees upfront via cryptocurrency. Legitimate employers cover hiring and background check costs; demanding crypto payments indicates fraud.

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: What type of sensitive data is targeted during pre-employment PII harvesting scams? PII is harvested to commit identity theft, open fraudulent credit lines, or breach accounts.

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: You receive an email from hr@microsoft-remote-careers.site inviting you to apply for an administrative position. How can you verify if this domain belongs to Microsoft? Always cross-reference job outreach domains against official corporate career portals.

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: How does the fake equipment check scam operate? The counterfeit check bounces after the victim has already transferred real personal funds to the scammer.

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: Scammers frequently copy authentic logos, employee photos, and executive names from LinkedIn to create convincing fake recruiter profiles. Copied branding assets build false credibility and lower applicant vigilance.

entries.title: Remote Recruitment, HR Impersonation & Onboarding Scams
entries.text: What is the primary risk of uploading your full unredacted driver's license or passport scan to an unverified job portal? Unredacted government IDs are primary assets used in identity fraud and unauthorized account creation.

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: What is the primary objective of a Business Email Compromise (BEC) attack targeting remote finance workers? BEC targets financial communications to divert payments to fraudulent accounts (Lazarus, 2024).

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: An email requesting an urgent update to a vendor's bank account details should always be verified by calling a phone number from the original master contract. Out-of-band verification using known contract phone numbers prevents invoice manipulation fraud.

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: A remote employee emails HR from john.smith-work@gmail.com asking to change their direct deposit bank account before Friday's payroll. What should HR do? Direct deposit changes sent via personal email accounts are primary targets for payroll interception.

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: Which of the following indicate that an invoice update request may be a BEC attempt? (Select TWO) Typosquatted domains and extreme artificial time pressure are indicators of BEC fraud.

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: Calling the phone number listed on a suspicious new invoice is a safe way to verify if the invoice's bank account changes are real. If the invoice is fake, the phone number on it leads directly to the scammer. Use trusted numbers from master contracts.

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: What internal financial control requires two separate individuals to review and approve wire transfers above a designated threshold? Dual-custody ensures that a single manipulated employee cannot execute unauthorized transfers alone.

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: A long-time vendor emails an invoice for $22,000. The invoice matches the expected amount, but a note says: "Our bank is undergoing an audit. Wire payment to our new overseas account." What is the safest response? Audit excuses for sudden overseas account changes are common BEC pretexts requiring verification.

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: In an email header, what field shows the actual mail server that sent the message, helping reveal domain spoofing? Email headers reveal true server origins, exposing sender address spoofing.

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: Business Email Compromise (BEC) attacks only use fake domains; they never involve real, compromised vendor email accounts. Attackers frequently compromise real vendor accounts (Vendor Email Compromise) to send fraudulent invoices from actual mailboxes.

entries.title: Remote BEC, Invoice Manipulation & Payment Fraud
entries.text: Why do BEC scammers target remote finance workers right before weekends or major holidays? Rushing before deadlines reduces vigilance, increasing the likelihood that security protocols will be skipped.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: What is the primary objective of an email phishing attack targeting remote employees? Email phishing uses deceptive messages to trick victims into sharing private credentials, executing malware, or surrendering sensitive organizational data.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: The presence of "HTTPS" and a padlock icon in the browser address bar guarantees that a login website is legitimate and safe. False. Threat actors can easily acquire free SSL/TLS certificates for fraudulent domain names, displaying HTTPS padlock icons on malicious credential-harvesting websites.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: What does the term "Quishing" refer to in modern cybersecurity? Quishing stands for QR code phishing, where malicious links are embedded in image files to bypass textual email filters.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: Which domain name represents an example of "typosquatting"? micros0ft-verify.com uses a zero ('0') in place of the letter 'o' to trick users into believing it is an official Microsoft communication channel.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: Security Email Gateways (SEGs) detect embedded QR code links just as easily as standard plain-text web links. False. Traditional SEGs primarily scan textual and HTML links. Image-based QR codes often bypass standard filters because the URL is hidden inside the graphic payload.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: Which of the following indicators strongly suggest that an email may be a phishing attempt? (Select ALL that apply) Mismatched headers, urgent MFA prompts, and macro-enabled attachments are classic phishing indicators. Digitally signed internal calendar invites are standard workflow items.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: You receive an email from IT-Support@company-desk.net stating: "Your password expires in 10 minutes. Click here to retain your current password." What should you do first? You should pause and verify unrequested urgent security alerts independently through official internal channels.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: Why do quishing attacks often succeed when targeting remote employees? Scanning QR codes on personal phones redirects traffic outside the desktop perimeter firewalls and email monitoring systems maintained by corporate networks.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: Hovering your mouse over a hyperlinked button in an email allows you to preview the actual destination URL before clicking. True. Hovering over a hyperlink reveals the true underlying web destination address in the browser or mail client status bar.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: Which of the following file extensions attached to an unsolicited email should be treated as high-risk? (Select ALL that apply) Double extensions (.pdf.exe), macro-enabled documents (.docm), and script files (.vbs) can automatically execute malicious payloads on a host computer.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: A remote freelancer receives an email with an embedded QR code labeled "Scan to View Signed Client NDA." Scans show the QR code opens http://192.168.1.1/login.html. Is this safe to open? False. Legitimate signed contracts are not hosted on raw local IP addresses or delivered via unencrypted QR codes without prior client agreement.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: What is the safest way to access a company cloud portal after receiving a suspicious email notification? Navigating independently via a trusted bookmark or manual URL entry completely bypasses any malicious redirects embedded in the email.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: Combosquatting involves adding words like "-security" or "-login" to legitimate brand names within a domain registration. True. Combosquatting merges legitimate brand trademarks with keywords (e.g., paypal-update-center.com) to mislead recipients.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: A virtual assistant receives an email displaying the company CEO’s exact name and profile photo. The sender address is ceo-office@exec-mail-corp.com (not the corporate @company.com domain). The message requests an urgent purchase of gift card vouchers for an ongoing client event. What social engineering tactic is being deployed? The attacker uses executive identity impersonation combined with a combosquatted external domain (exec-mail-corp.com) to trick the assistant into making unauthorized purchases.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: What technical security mechanisms can organizations configure to help block spoofed email headers? (Select ALL that apply) SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are DNS-based email authentication protocols configured to verify sender domain legitimacy and stop header spoofing.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: You scan a QR code from a vendor PDF. It opens a Google Sign-In page asking you to "Grant Full OAuth Permissions to App XYZ." Granting access is safe because the URL starts with accounts.google.com. False. Malicious OAuth applications use real Google/Microsoft sign-in portals to request excessive account permissions. Once granted, the attacker gets persistent cloud access without needing your password.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: What is the primary reason threat actors exploit human curiosity or urgency during a phishing attempt? High-pressure emotional triggers (fear, urgency, curiosity) induce cognitive overload, causing targets to act before inspecting sender details or verifying requests.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: A remote software engineer receives an email containing a link to a "Critical Security Patch" hosted on github-downloads-security.net. What is the most rigorous way to confirm if this patch is legitimate? Internal verification via official out-of-band communication channels is the only reliable way to confirm patch validity.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: If you realize you entered your corporate credentials into a fake login portal 5 minutes ago, what immediate steps must you execute? (Select ALL that apply) Resetting credentials, revoking active sessions, alerting IT, and auditing registered MFA devices stops ongoing unauthorized account access. Deleting local browser history does not stop the remote attacker.

entries.title: Quishing
entries.text: Phishing attacks targeting remote employees exclusively occur through traditional business email, never through personal email or instant messaging platforms. False. Attackers routinely target remote employees across personal email, LinkedIn DMs, WhatsApp, and Telegram to bypass enterprise email controls. MODULE 2: Spear Phishing

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: How does spear phishing differ from generic mass phishing? Spear phishing relies on prior reconnaissance to tailor realistic messages directly to specific targets.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: What does the acronym "OSINT" stand for in cybersecurity reconnaissance? OSINT stands for Open Source Intelligence, referring to publicly available data mined from social platforms, repositories, and directories.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: Public professional profiles on LinkedIn can provide attackers with information used to craft spear phishing messages. True. Attackers mine job titles, reporting structures, vendor software, and current projects from LinkedIn profiles to build convincing pretexts.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: Why do attackers often send password-protected .zip files containing malicious attachments? Email gateway scanners cannot inspect encrypted archive contents without the password, allowing malicious payloads past boundary defenses.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: Enabling macros on an unverified Microsoft Word or Excel attachment is safe as long as the document has a .docm extension. False. The .docm extension explicitly denotes a macro-enabled document. Enabling macros runs underlying VBA code that can install malware.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: Which public sources are commonly harvested by adversaries during the OSINT phase of a spear phishing campaign? (Select ALL that apply) LinkedIn, GitHub, and social media posts provide open public data. Private encrypted database servers are not public OSINT sources.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: You are a remote graphic designer. You receive a direct message on Telegram from someone claiming to be a senior manager at your main client account, asking you to open Design_Brief.pdf.exe. How should you react? Files ending in .exe are executable programs. The .pdf.exe naming convention tricks users into opening executable malware.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: Spear phishing attempts only target executive leadership (CEOs/CFOs), never entry-level remote contractors or virtual assistants. False. Attackers regularly target contractors, virtual assistants, and junior personnel as initial footholds to access corporate networks or facilitate payment fraud.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: What operating system settings and user habits help defend against weaponized spear phishing attachments? (Select ALL that apply) Revealing full file extensions, blocking Office macros, and out-of-band verification mitigate attachment risks. Running untrusted files as Administrator increases security risks.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: A spear phisher notices on Twitter that your company’s Lead Developer is on a 14-hour flight. The attacker emails you posing as the Lead Developer, requesting emergency production database credentials. Should you comply? False. Attackers exploit travel schedules to create situations where the spoofed identity cannot be reached easily. Always follow established verification protocols.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: What technical feature makes MITRE ATT&CK Technique T1566.001 particularly dangerous to enterprise endpoint security? Technique T1566.001 relies on social engineering to trick the user into executing malicious attachments locally.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: Reducing the amount of detailed operational information shared on public social media accounts helps reduce your exposure to OSINT reconnaissance. True. Practicing digital footprint hygiene limits the intelligence attackers can use to build spear phishing lures.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: Spear phishers only target executives; entry-level remote contractors are never targeted because they lack system permissions. Entry-level contractors are frequently targeted as initial access points to pivot deeper into enterprise networks or harvest credentials.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: Which of the following indicate that a project brief attachment might be a spear-phishing payload? *(Select TWO)* Macro-enabled files (.xlsm) and disk image archives (.iso) disguised as documents are common malicious delivery formats.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: What information can an attacker gather from your public GitHub profile to make a spear-phishing email believable? Public GitHub repositories display technical environments, active projects, and peer collaborators.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: A freelancer receives a high-paying offer on Upwork. The client insists on sending an .iso file containing "project assets" before contract signing. Why is this suspicious? ISO files are container formats used by attackers to deliver malware while evading basic security filters.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: Spear phishing relies solely on technical software exploits and does not use psychological manipulation. Spear phishing is a socio-technical attack combining technical delivery vectors with psychological manipulation (trust, urgency, authority).

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: What step should you take before opening a password-protected .zip file from an external party? Verifying the source through another channel and inspecting files securely prevents payload execution.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: What term describes altering sender details so an email appears to come from a legitimate internal colleague? Email spoofing manipulates header fields (From:) to impersonate legitimate contacts.

entries.title: Spear Phishing
entries.text: An email claiming to be from your company's HR department contains a link to "Updated W-2 Tax Forms." The link URL points to http://hr-portal.tax-verify-auth.com. What is the safest course of action? Identifying external, non-company domain names by hovering over links helps detect phishing portals before entering credentials. MODULE 3: Smishing

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: What does the term "Smishing" stand for? Smishing combines "SMS" (text messaging) and "phishing".

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: If a text message appears in the same chat thread as previous legitimate bank messages, it is 100% guaranteed to be safe. Attackers can use Sender ID spoofing to inject fake text messages into existing SMS conversation threads on mobile devices.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: You receive a text message: *"USPS Alert: Your package cannot be delivered due to an incorrect house number. Update info here: bit.ly/3xY9zQ"*. You are expecting a package. What is the correct action? Always verify parcel delivery alerts by accessing the official website or app independently, never through unsolicited SMS links.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: Why are mobile browsers particularly vulnerable to web link deceptive techniques? Reduced screen size makes it difficult for users to inspect the full domain path of a link before interacting.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: Which of the following are primary indicators of a smishing attempt? *(Select TWO)* Unsolicited prize claims and requests to text back MFA tokens are key smishing indicators.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: Replying "STOP" to a smishing text message from an unknown scammer will safely unsubscribe you from their list. Replying to a scam text confirms to the attacker that your phone number is active, leading to more targeted attacks.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: You attempt to log into your work portal. A minute later, you receive a text: *"IT Helpdesk: We detected an abnormal login. Reply YES with the code you just received to block the login."* What is happening? Attackers trigger a real login prompt to generate a genuine OTP, then smish the victim to forward that OTP to complete the breach.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: What is the risk of using shortened URLs (bit.ly, tinyurl) in SMS messages? URL shorteners hide the real destination address, concealing malicious domains.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: Personal smartphones used under BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) policies are always protected by corporate firewalls. Personal BYOD devices operate on commercial cellular networks or home Wi-Fi, bypassing corporate perimeter firewalls.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: What technology allows scammers to change the phone number or name displayed on your mobile incoming text screen? Sender ID spoofing allows SMS gateways to modify the header sender text displayed on receiver phones.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: A remote worker receives a text message: *"HR ALERT: Update your direct deposit bank details at* *https://payroll-portal-update.com* *before 5 PM to receive this week's paycheck."* What should the worker check first? Urgent threats regarding payroll/direct deposit sent via text require out-of-band verification.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: What shortcode number can users in many regions forward spam or smishing texts to for reporting? Forwarding spam texts to 7726 (SPAM) alerts carriers to investigate and block malicious sender numbers.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: Legitimate banks routinely send text messages asking customers to directly text back their full PIN or password. Financial institutions explicitly prohibit requesting sensitive passwords, PINs, or OTPs via text.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: Which mobile security practice best protects against smishing attacks seeking to compromise work accounts? Authenticator apps generate time-based codes locally, rendering SMS interception attacks useless.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: You receive a WhatsApp text from an unknown international number displaying your company logo: *"Hi, I am John from Corporate IT. We are updating mobile profiles. Click this link to install our security certificate."* How should you respond? Corporate IT security profiles are deployed through formal Mobile Device Management (MDM) tools, never random instant messages.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: Advanced smishing kits can deploy mobile malware that automatically reads incoming SMS verification codes and forwards them to a remote C2 server. Malicious mobile applications (e.g., infected APKs) can request SMS permissions to intercept and exfiltrate OTPs.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: What is the safest action to take when receiving a suspicious text message? Refraining from interaction and deleting/reporting the message mitigates risk.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: A text message reads: *"Bank Alert: Fraud detected. Call 1-800-555-0199 immediately to cancel the transaction."* What is the safest way to call your bank? Phone numbers in smishing texts often lead directly to vishing agents; always use official contact numbers.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: Why do attackers target mobile devices rather than desktop computers in smishing campaigns? *(Select TWO)* Mobile devices combine rapid user response habits with weaker endpoint monitoring compared to managed corporate desktops.

entries.title: Smishing
entries.text: Legitimate logistics companies will always require you to pay a re-delivery fee via a third-party link sent by SMS. Demanding credit card details via SMS links for "unclaimed parcels" is a standard smishing lure. MODULE 4: Vishing

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: What is "Vishing"? Vishing is social engineering delivered via voice/phone communication.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Caller ID information displayed on a smartphone screen can be easily spoofed by attackers using web VoIP services. Caller ID metadata can be modified by outbound VoIP gateways to show fake names and numbers.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: You receive a call from "Corporate IT Support" stating your laptop is infected. The caller instructs you to go to a website and install AnyDesk so they can clean the machine. What should you do? Installing remote desktop software on unsolicited calls gives attackers full control over your endpoint.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Why is voice interaction (vishing) particularly effective at tricking targets compared to email? Live dialogue creates urgency and emotional pressure, making critical analysis difficult.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Which of the following information should you NEVER read aloud or share during an inbound phone call? *(Select TWO)* Passwords and OTPs must remain confidential and should never be disclosed over inbound calls.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Official company helpdesks frequently call remote workers unannounced to demand their personal email passwords. Legitimate helpdesks do not require your private account passwords to perform administrative tasks.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: An incoming call displays your bank's exact toll-free phone number. The caller states: *"Security Alert: A $900 transfer was attempted. Read the code we just sent your phone to cancel it."* What should you do? Spoofed Caller ID makes fake calls appear genuine; hanging up and calling back independently confirms authenticity.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: What term describes repeated, automated MFA push prompts sent to a user’s phone to force them into tapping "Approve" out of frustration? Push bombing bombards targets with MFA prompts until they accidentally or reactively accept one.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Interactive Voice Response (IVR) robocall systems are only used by legitimate companies and cannot be set up by cybercriminals. Attackers frequently create automated IVR phone trees to imitate official bank menus before transferring victims to live scammers.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: What is the primary objective of a vishing attacker who convinces a remote employee to install Quick Assist or TeamViewer? Remote administration tools grant full desktop GUI control to the adversary.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: A caller claims to be from the internal finance team: *"I am processing your remote equipment reimbursement, but the system is throwing an error. What is your full bank account and routing number?"* How should you respond? Financial distribution updates must follow encrypted, formal portal workflows rather than verbal disclosures.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: What is the best immediate response when an unknown caller becomes aggressive and demands immediate compliance? Aggressive emotional pressure is a hallmark of vishing; hanging up terminates the attack vector.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Vishing attacks only target personal landline phones and cannot be conducted over corporate VoIP applications like Microsoft Teams or Zoom. Attackers can initiate vishing via corporate VoIP, direct web calls, or messaging applications.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Which technique helps mitigate the risk of Caller ID spoofing when receiving unexpected internal calls? Calling back via a independently verified number bypasses spoofed inbound routing.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: You receive an unexpected call: *"This is Executive Assistant Claire calling on behalf of CEO Mark. He needs you to purchase five digital gift cards right now for a client meeting."* What red flag is present? Requesting gift cards under executive pressure is a classic social engineering financial scam.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Generative AI tools now allow vishing attackers to clone an executive's voice using short audio samples taken from public videos or webinars. AI voice cloning enables realistic synthetic audio impersonation of targeted individuals.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: What should a remote worker do if they accidentally approve a fraudulent MFA push prompt during a vishing call? Swift incident reporting enables security teams to isolate compromised sessions before lateral movement occurs.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Which department should a remote employee contact to report a suspicious vishing call impersonating internal staff? Security teams handle threat logging, account isolation, and incident analysis.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: Which of the following indicators suggest an incoming phone call is a vishing attempt? *(Select TWO)* Emergency protocol bypasses and requests for passcodes are primary vishing tactics.

entries.title: Vishing
entries.text: An official bank representative will hang up on you if you state that you are hanging up to call back via the number on your payment card. Legitimate representatives encourage safe verification habits and welcome callbacks to official lines. MODULE 5: Pretexting

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: What is the primary characteristic of a pretexting attack? Pretexting centers on creating a plausible false persona and narrative.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: Pretexting attacks always happen within a single 30-second interaction and never involve multi-day conversations. Pretexting often uses a "slow-burn" approach, building rapport across multiple days or weeks.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: Someone claiming to be an "External ISO Auditor" contacts a remote worker asking for a complete list of internal server IP addresses. The caller says opening an IT ticket will take too long. What should the worker do? Never bypass formal verification and ticketing procedures for external inquiries.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: Why do pretexters often try to discourage victims from submitting official IT service tickets? Formal ticketing creates an audit trail that alerts legitimate security personnel.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: Which of the following personas are common disguises used in pretexting campaigns? *(Select TWO)* Pretexters assume roles that invoke authority (auditor) or empathy (distressed colleague).

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: Pretexting relies heavily on human psychological traits like helpfulness, politeness, and respect for authority. Attackers exploit natural human social tendencies to manipulate targets.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: You receive a message from a "new vendor" asking for internal directory structures so they can "prepare project integration." You have not received any notification from management about a new vendor. What is the correct protocol? Unverified third parties must be vetted through management before receiving internal assets.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: How does pretexting differ from mass phishing? Pretexting prioritizes narrative depth and trust over volume.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: A pretexter will never use public information from LinkedIn to build their fake story. Pretexters extensively use OSINT from LinkedIn and company sites to make their scenarios believable.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: What term describes an attacker engaging a victim in casual conversation over several days to establish a sense of normal friendship before executing a scam? Slow-burn pretexting grooms the victim over time to lower security vigilance.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: A remote contractor receives an email from someone claiming to be "Head of Global Security": *"We are running a silent security exercise. Do not inform your supervisor. Send your current VPN credentials directly to this email."* What should the contractor do? Demands for secrecy and credential submission are major red flags; legitimate security exercises do not collect user passwords via email.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: What structural control prevents pretexting attempts from compromising internal resources? Formal channels and strict verification neutralize pretexting narratives.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: Pretexters never target remote workers who do not have executive titles. Administrative assistants, support staff, and contractors are frequently targeted for their access to directory data and internal processes.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: Which conversational signs suggest an interaction may be a pretexting attempt? *(Select TWO)* Bypassing procedures and using high-emotion stories are common pretexting tactics.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: What should you do if an external party claiming to be an auditor asks for employee home addresses? Personally Identifiable Information (PII) disclosures must be handled exclusively by authorized departments.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: Pretexting can occur over email, phone calls, social media, or messaging apps. Pretexting is medium-agnostic and occurs across any communication channel.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: A remote worker receives a call from an individual claiming to be a printer technician needing internal Wi-Fi passwords to fix an office printer 500 miles away. Why is this request suspicious? Evaluating the logical plausibility of a request helps spot flawed pretexts.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: What role does flattery play in pretexting interactions? Flattery creates positive rapport, encouraging the target to comply with requests.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: Out-of-band verification is ineffective against pretexting. Independent out-of-band verification effectively exposes pretexts by contacting the real organization or individual.

entries.title: Pretexting
entries.text: What is the gold standard rule when handling requests for sensitive corporate information? Always verify identity and clearance before transmitting sensitive data. MODULE 6: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Env

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: Why is SMS-based Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) considered less secure than authenticator apps? SMS relies on vulnerable cellular protocols subject to interception and SIM swaps.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: Connecting a remote work laptop to an isolated "Guest Network" on your home router helps protect work data from compromised smart home IoT devices. Guest networks isolate work devices from unpatched IoT appliances on the main subnet.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: You accidentally enter your work password on a suspicious website landing page. What is the FIRST technical action you should take? Disconnecting limits malware/session exfiltration, and immediate reporting allows rapid password/session revocation.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: What is the risk of keeping factory default administrative credentials on your home Wi-Fi router? Botnets and attackers target default router passwords to gain network control.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: Which of the following authentication methods provide resistance against phishing attacks? *(Select TWO)* FIDO2 keys and TOTP authenticator apps are significantly more secure than plain passwords or SMS.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: Postponing operating system security updates for several months improves laptop battery performance and network security. Unpatched operating systems leave known security vulnerabilities exposed to software exploits.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: A client emails asking you to wire project funds to a new bank account. The email comes from the client's real address. What is the safest out-of-band verification step? Always verify banking detail changes via an independent, trusted communication channel.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: What is the primary purpose of a Password Manager for remote workers? Password managers eliminate password reuse across multiple corporate and personal sites.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: Using the same password across both personal personal banking and corporate work portals is acceptable as long as the password contains at least 8 letters. Password reuse enables credential stuffing: if one site is breached, attackers try the credentials across all accounts.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: Which wireless encryption standard provides the strongest security for home Wi-Fi networks? WPA3 is the current state-of-the-art Wi-Fi encryption standard.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: You are working remotely from a coffee shop. What tool should you use to encrypt your internet traffic before connecting to the open public Wi-Fi? VPNs create an encrypted tunnel that protects data from eavesdropping on unencrypted public Wi-Fi networks.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: What should you do with unused smart home devices connected to your primary work Wi-Fi network? Isolating or hardening smart devices prevents them from serving as entry points to work machines.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: An incognito or private browsing window completely protects your computer from downloading malware. Incognito mode prevents local browser history storage; it does not block malware downloads or network attacks.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: Which actions are part of solid remote work cyber hygiene? *(Select TWO)* Regular software patching and Wi-Fi encryption are fundamental security practices.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: You notice a USB flash drive sitting on your home office desk. You do not remember buying it or where it came from. What should you do? Unknown USB drives (baiting) can execute hardware-level keystroke injection or malware scripts.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: Reporting a security mistake immediately to your IT team is better than hiding it, because swift response minimizes organizational damage. Early reporting allows security teams to revoke compromised tokens before lateral movement occurs.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: What feature in web browsers helps protect users from accessing known malicious websites? Browser reputation filters warn users before navigating to flagged phishing or malware domains.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: What is the safest way to store physical backup codes for your account MFA? MFA backup codes grant full account recovery access and must be protected like primary passwords.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: Which steps should be taken when setting up a personal BYOD smartphone for remote work access? *(Select TWO)* Lock screen controls and security software prevent physical and unauthorized software access.

entries.title: Essential Safe Practices for Remote Environments
entries.text: In a remote work environment, cybersecurity is solely the responsibility of corporate IT staff, and individual employees play no role in defense. Without traditional enterprise perimeters, individual remote workers serve as the primary line of defense against social engineering attacks.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: You receive an email from your bank asking you to verify your account by clicking a link. What should you do? Never click links in unsolicited emails. Contact the bank through official channels.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: Which of these is a common sign of a phishing email? Phishing emails often use urgency, generic greetings, and suspicious sender addresses.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: An email claims your account will be locked unless you act within 15 minutes. What is this technique called? Creating artificial urgency is a common social engineering tactic to bypass critical thinking.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: How does spear phishing differ from regular phishing? Spear phishing is highly targeted, using personal information to appear legitimate.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: A colleague sends you an urgent request to transfer funds to a new account. What should you verify first? Always verify urgent requests through a different channel (phone call, in-person) before taking action.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: You receive an email from your CEO asking for sensitive company data, addressed to you by name. What should you do? Spear phishing often impersonates executives. Always verify through a separate channel.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: What is vishing? Vishing uses phone calls to deceive victims into revealing sensitive information.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: You receive a call from "tech support" claiming your computer is infected. They ask for remote access. What should you do? Legitimate tech support never makes unsolicited calls asking for remote access.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: A caller claims to be from the IRS and demands immediate payment via gift cards. What should you do? Government agencies never demand payment via gift cards. This is a classic vishing scam.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: What is smishing? Smishing uses text messages to trick victims into clicking malicious links or sharing information.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: You receive a text message claiming you won a prize and need to click a link to claim it. What should you do? Unsolicited prize claims via text are almost always smishing scams.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: You receive a text from your bank asking you to verify a transaction by clicking a link. What should you do? Banks never ask you to click links in text messages. Always use official contact methods.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: What is pretexting? Pretexting involves inventing a fabricated scenario to manipulate victims into revealing information.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: Someone claiming to be from IT asks for your password to "fix your account." What should you do? Legitimate IT staff never ask for passwords. Report this immediately.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: A delivery person asks for your name and birth date to verify a package. What should you do? Legitimate delivery services do not need personal information like birth dates to verify packages.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: What is quishing? Quishing uses QR codes to direct victims to malicious websites or download malware.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: You see a QR code on a flyer promising a free gift. What should you do before scanning? Always verify the source of QR codes and use security-aware scanners.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: Which password practice is most secure? Password managers generate and store unique, complex passwords for each account.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: What is two-factor authentication (2FA)? 2FA requires something you know (password) and something you have (code, device).

entries.title: Cybersecurity Awareness Assessment
entries.text: You receive a file attachment from an unknown sender. What should you do? Never open attachments from unknown senders. Delete immediately.
